name: SNOW IRON GATE
desc: Snow falls steady against iron. The gate looms ahead — old metal gone gray with frost, chains thick as your arm. You've been walking through cold you can't name, following a path you can't explain. Your paws are numb. Your breath clouds the air. Something pulled you forward — not hunger, not anger, not revenge. Just... forward. Like your feet knew something your head didn't. Now the gate stands before you, held by more than metal. Boars shift in the snow behind two ferrets who stand front and center like they own this place. Rabbits dart between their legs, twitching. One ferret snorts. 'Hah — a fox? On the Path of the Samurai? Go home, kit.' The other doesn't laugh. He just looks at you — really looks — waiting. The snow keeps falling. And somewhere under the doubt, under the cold, there's a quiet thing that refuses to turn around.
clear_desc: The ferrets go quiet. One laughs despite himself — low, surprised, almost respectful. 'Not bad, fox.' Snow settles on all of you. You're standing, they're not — and that means something. But more than that: you notice how *they* moved. Not fast. Efficient. Every step placed just so, no wasted motion — like they'd decided where to be before arriving. While you swung at rabbits and shoved past boars, the ferrets were already *elsewhere*. That's what you forgot. The lesson you let go cold. Quick Steps. You're going to need that. The gate groans open. Wind cuts through sharp and clean. Beyond it, the path stretches into white nothing — trees, shadows, more fights, more questions. You step forward. Still confused. Still not turning back.

lines.text: Scouts spotted <hl>Ferret Clan</hl> banners near the keep gate.
Then we settle this the old way.
